title: Plan data goes in, a guided session and updated weights come out

parts.name: Plan data (plan.json)
parts.description: The approved 12-week plan as data: three lift sessions with ordered blocks, every exercise's sets, rep range, effort target and rest, the stretch block, run definitions, the weekday calendar and the week phases. Changing the plan means editing this file and publishing a new version; no code changes. v1.4 adds a tempo and focus cues to every exercise and a goal sentence to every session. v1.5: exercises that use two dumbbells are marked pair, and every curl is named by type. v1.9: data/goals.json holds the ranked goals for the Plan tab, and data/muscles.json maps each exercise to muscle groups.

parts.name: Settings (settings.json)
parts.description: Defaults for cues (vibrate, beep, warning tick), screen wake lock, transition seconds, start date and bodyweight. Cameron's changes in the Settings screen are stored in IndexedDB on top of these defaults. v1.5: confirmSetup toggles the Set-up done tap before each new block. v1.18: Loud beeps (with a Play the beep button), Set times follow my pace (adaptTiming) with a list of what was learned and Start over; the Set-up done switch now covers every exercise, each bar change and the stretches.

parts.name: Cameron's taps
lines: Start, Done, edit a set, review,
parts.description: Everything Cameron does in the app: start a session, tap Done on a set, edit weight/reps/RPE, pause, skip a step, go back one step, trim to fit, end early, fill the run form, edit a target, back up, export, restore. v1.9: coach check-ins on the Plan tab: a note with quick tags (Too heavy, Too light, Rest too long, Need more rest, Pain, Slept badly, Felt good). Weight tags move that lift's next target one step; rest tags move its rest 15 s, at most 45 s either way (settings.restAdjust, applied by the Session Builder). v1.14: every press gives a short buzz on Android (follows the vibrate setting); long-press the app icon for Today, Runs and Progress shortcuts.

parts.name: Garmin runs
lines: activities from the watch, by way
of a job in your private repo
parts.description: Optional (v1.10). Garmin's personal API lets Cameron read his own activities with a key he creates in Garmin Connect. The key is saved as a secret in his private GitHub repo, where a small job (data/garmin-job.yml, added to that repo during set-up) asks Garmin every two hours, and whenever the app saves garmin-request.json there, and writes garmin-activities.json with the location fields dropped. The phone reads that file through the same token sync uses and adds what is new to the run log: runs, ski days and long bike or rower sessions (rules.json garmin.types). A run typed in by hand on the same day takes the watch's numbers instead of being logged twice, a deleted Garmin run stays out, and type, effort and notes are never overwritten. The key is never on the phone, in the app or in a backup. A computer set to Only views never adds runs; it shows them after the phone uploads. From v1.12 to v1.18.0 the app decided which planned run a Garmin run was. v1.18.1 (Cameron, Nov 21: "make me log it to take credit"): a run from Garmin comes in as an easy run and counts toward the week's miles; it counts for a planned run only when Cameron taps Count it (on the planned run's card on the Runs tab or Home, or in the run sheet) or picks its type; Side run keeps it an easy run that is not asked about again. A ski day still counts for the long run by itself, as the plan says (rules.json garmin.types countsForPlan); a bike or rower session waits for the tap like a run. Cameron's own pick of type always sticks.

parts.name: Rules (rules.json)
parts.description: Progression rules as data: weight increments per lift, the success test (all sets at the top of the range at RPE 8 or lower), the accessory rule (reps first, then the smallest jump), the stall rule (three flat sessions in a row take 5% off; two misses and 10% until v1.18.1), baseline weeks, phase overrides (week 7 half sets, weeks 8-11 at 3-5 reps, week 12 retest), ramp-up steps, trim order and timing estimates. v1.4 adds set timing (tempo default, margin, set-up seconds by equipment, get-ready seconds), the effort scale behind the four effort buttons (stored as RPE 6, 8, 9, 10), and rough starting-weight estimates for free-weight accessories. v1.5: dumbbellPairs (pair lifts are stored as totals and jump two dumbbell steps), timing.confirmSetup (wait for a tap before each new block), review.blockSaveOnOpenItems, weighted pull-up jump 5 lb. v1.8: catchUp (warm-up, rest for a lone superset exercise, stretch on or off). v1.18: timing.confirmSetup per exercise, confirmWeightChange (bar changes wait for a tap), confirmBeforeBlocks (stretch and Engine wait for Ready), change-over seconds between sides and between stretches, gymAwayMinutes; cues (how loud each beep is and its notes); pacing (when set and set-up times follow Cameron's pace). v1.18.1 (rulesVersion 1.9, rules R4 that Cameron approved on Nov 20): stall holds sessionsBeforeDrop, dropFraction, flatAtRpe and resetReps (v1.18.2, rulesVersion 1.9.1: flatAtRpe null, Cameron's pick, so only missed reps make a session flat; 9 would count a Hard or Maxed set too); phases.heavy.startWeightFactor sets the heavy-week start; garmin.types countsForPlan lets a ski day count for the long run without a tap.

parts.name: Session Builder
parts.description: Expands a session from plan.json into a flat, ordered list of steps: warm-up holds, ramp-up sets, work sets, rests, superset alternation (B1 set, short rest, B2 set, longer rest), finisher rounds, dead hangs, transitions, stretches. Fills each set's target weight and reps from the saved targets, applies the week's phase (baseline, light, heavy, retest) and estimates each step's planned seconds for the clock. Since v1.4 a set's seconds come from its reps and the exercise's tempo (plan.json) plus a margin, and every set has a countdown in front of it: the rest before it, a set-up step sized by equipment before an exercise's first set, or a short switch step inside finisher rounds. v1.18: uses the seconds per rep and the set-up seconds that Pacing learned for an exercise in place of the plan's. A set done one side at a time is timed for both sides plus a change-over. A stretch done per side is one step with the change-over inside it, and a short change-over step sits between stretches. The countdowns in front of sets can be rebuilt during a session (after Equipment taken), so each exercise's first set keeps its set-up time.

parts.name: Player
parts.description: Walks the timeline one step at a time. Timers are computed from timestamps so they stay right when the screen locks. Vibrates and beeps when a rest ends, keeps the screen awake, shows planned vs projected finish and how far ahead or behind the session is, and offers Trim to fit (preview, then confirm). Each work set shows last session's result for that exercise. Logging a set runs a live PR check against the stored bests (estimated 1RM, heaviest weight) and gives a haptic tap. When the app is in the background during a rest, it asks the service worker to fire a notification at the end time. Pause, back and end early live behind the menu button; the in-progress session is saved on every step so it can be resumed. Since v1.4 a work set ends on its own timer and is logged at its target; the rest screen that follows shows the set just done with four effort buttons and a tap-to-fix weight and reps. The last 5 seconds before every set are a get-ready count (amber screen, ticks, the coming set spoken aloud). A pace bar shows which rep the tempo puts you on. The screen is green for work, blue for rest. Back and Pause are on the screen. Voice and auto-advance can be switched off in Settings. v1.5: Pause is in the header on every step with a tap-to-resume banner; the countdown before the first set of a new block holds until Set-up done is tapped; Equipment taken moves a later block to now and puts the current one right after it; in a finisher the top bar lists its exercises; the last-set card has - and + for weight and reps and a Logged / Saved check; two-dumbbell lifts show the total with 2 x each. v1.18 (Cameron's notes from his third workout): the screen is a fixed shell that fits one phone screen; the middle gives up lines and size in four steps before anything scrolls, and every weight is sized to its box. Header: Plan, the gym clock, Pause and the menu (Back one step moved into the menu); under it the block, the lift and the set on one line, then a strip with one letter per block. The gym clock counts from Start and keeps running through a pause; a pause turns the screen and the Pause button red and shows how long it has lasted. The countdown before the first set of each exercise, before a barbell set whose weight changed, and before the stretches and the Engine waits for a tap (Set-up done or Ready); a tap during a rest keeps the rest. The rest screen lists the coming sets with weight and reps, and Plan opens the whole session with every set, its weight and a tick. A set, hold or stretch done one side at a time shows a Left and a Right box with their own clocks and colors, beeps at the change-over and says the side. Beeps are a louder square tone (rules.json cues, Settings > Loud beeps) and the voice says reps and weight. Equipment taken also swaps the exercises inside a finisher. The last-set card shows after the last set of a block too. A set the timer logged with no effort tapped is marked unconfirmed, with no effort lit on its card, until an effort is tapped (new numbers alone leave it unconfirmed). The set screen shows the numbers Done or the timer will log: typed in Edit and hidden, or logged before Back one step, else the target. A session left open past timing.resumeWindowHours with sets logged is offered to save or discard instead of Resume. Each set records how long it took against its timer, and each first set how long the set-up took, for Pacing. A second tap on the main button within 0.6 s is ignored, Right can be tapped once the left side has started, and a set run again after Back one step keeps what it was logged or corrected with.

parts.name: Logger
lines: one tap logs weight, reps, RPE
parts.description: Records each set: Done accepts the pre-filled target weight and reps; Edit opens weight, reps and RPE. When the session ends it opens the Review screen: every exercise with its sets (tap to correct), the engine's verdict (Up / Hold / Drop / Set) with its reason, and the next weight and reps as editable fields; Save runs the engine on the corrected sets, applies any overrides (tagged 'set by you') and stores the session. Then the summary. The run log form moved to the Runs page in v1.10. v1.5: the Review screen lists skipped sets and sets missing a weight or reps first and keeps Save locked until each is filled in or confirmed as skipped. v1.14: Session done shows sets, minutes and volume against the same session last time, records with a badge, the week's rings, and Save image (js/share-card.js draws the card on the phone and opens the Android share sheet; nothing is uploaded). v1.16: a number that looks wrong (a barbell weight under the empty bar, half or less of the target, half again over it, or reps far past the range) is held for a second look. In the workout Done shows an amber note and keeps the set until Cameron fixes it or taps Done again; on the Review screen flagged sets are listed first and keep Save locked until fixed or confirmed; Home shows a Check these numbers card for saved sessions, whose fix sheet rewrites the weights and recomputes that lift's target, records and what-changed (js/sanity.js; limits in rules.json numberCheck). v1.18: the session record keeps the time in the gym (start to finish, pauses included) next to the working time; Session done shows both when there was a pause. Sets the timer logged with no effort tapped are listed on Review as logged by the timer and shown as not rated; a tap rates or corrects one (new numbers alone keep it not rated), They all went as planned confirms them all, and Save does not wait for them. The finished session is stored as soon as it ends and until Save (a reload or a closed app comes back to Review; Home shows Not saved yet; a new session waits for it; one that came back can be discarded), and Save saves it once. Reps below 0, part of a rep and weights below 0 are refused where they are typed. v1.18.1: a set the timer logged can be rated after Save too, on the summary (Rate on the set, or Rate the set the timer logged) or on the session in Progress; when that session is the lift's latest and the last set is rated, the lift's next target is worked out again, otherwise the target stays and a toast says why (a later session, or a target he or the coach set since; a number fix follows the same rule). The session record keeps targetsBefore, the targets it started from.

parts.name: Progression Engine
lines: applies rules after review and save
parts.description: Runs once after a session saves. For each exercise in the session: applies the week override if any, the baseline rule in weeks 1-2, otherwise the success test (main lifts) or the reps-then-weight rule (accessories), counts flat sessions and takes 5% off after three in a row (v1.18.1; 10% after two misses before), computes Epley estimated 1RM for benchmark lifts, writes the new targets and a plain-language what-changed line per exercise. Power clean is excluded from automatic progression. Also keeps each exercise's best estimated 1RM and heaviest weight and reports personal records when a session beats them. v1.5: incrementFor doubles the jump for pair lifts; starting estimates for pair lifts are totals. v1.18: a lift with a set the timer logged before an effort was picked (unconfirmed) and saved without a rating keeps its target and stall count for the next session (rules R4, rule 1). v1.18.1 (rules R4 from the Nov 20 plan review, checked against its reference engine): a main lift moves up a rep, or a step at the top of its range, when every set is made at RPE 8 or under; a flat session is a miss at the target weight (v1.18.2: only missed reps, Cameron's pick; rules.json stall.flatAtRpe 9 would count a Hard or Maxed set too); week 2 never counts flat; the first heavy-week session of each main lift starts 5% over the target it had going in, at 3 reps, once per lift (the target keeps a heavyStart mark). The power clean is never raised: its target follows the doubles he did, and it trains at its benchmark weight, not 90% of it. Accessories have no flat count. The result keeps `before`, each lift's target as the session found it, which the session stores as targetsBefore; js/sanity.js rerunLift works one lift out again from there after a number fix or a rating after Save (rule 12), so a fix in week 8 or 9 keeps the flat count and the heavy start. The v1.19 all-out check will sit on the outcome before the target is written (rule 13).

parts.name: Catch-up list
parts.description: Works out what is still owed this week from the saved sessions: sets that were skipped or never reached (a session ended early), minus any already made up, plus whole lifts whose day has passed with nothing logged. Sets cut by Trim to fit and the if-time block are not owed, and nothing carries past Sunday. From the leftover sets it builds a Catch-up session (short warm-up, the owed blocks in plan order, stretch) that the Session Builder turns into a timeline like any other. On a Slack day it takes the today card on Home; on other days it shows as Owed this week. Catch-up sets are logged and count for records; they move a target only for an exercise the original session never logged. Settings are in rules.json under catchUp. v1.18.1 (rules R4 rule 11): a skipped set never adds to the flat count, so making it up takes nothing back.

parts.name: Storage and offline cache
parts.description: IndexedDB holds targets (with per-exercise bests for PR checks), sessions, runs, what-changed lists, settings overrides and the in-progress session. The service worker caches the app's files under a versioned cache name so it opens with no signal, picks up a new version on the next open with signal, and shows the rest-end notification when the page asks it to while in the background. Backup writes a JSON file with everything; Restore reads one back. v1.5: a pairTotals flag records whether older per-dumbbell numbers were doubled; the app asks once when it finds them, and a restored pre-v1.5 backup asks again. v1.18: a finished session waiting on Review is kept under its own key until it is saved or discarded (not in backups). v1.18.1: kv dataVersion holds the app version the stored data was last upgraded for, and js/upgrade.js runs each one-time upgrade once: on open, after a restore and after the computer loads the phone's copy. The 1.18.1 upgrade sets every flat count to 0 (rules R4 rule 11) and turns Garmin runs the app had given a planned run into easy runs waiting for Count it. replaceTarget swaps one whole target (a number fix or a rating after Save).

parts.name: Pacing
parts.description: New in v1.18 (Cameron: adjust the time when he keeps ending early or pausing). Reads the saved sessions and works out, per exercise, the seconds per rep and the set-up seconds he actually uses. A set counts as early when he taps Done with time to spare, late when he adds 15 s or pauses during it and still uses its time (a pause and an early Done is a break, not slow reps). At most a minute of a pause counts as set-up time. After 3 sets of an exercise in a row the same way its set time follows him, kept between half and 1.75 times the plan's tempo; a lift marked keepTempo in plan.json (the calf raise pause) is never shortened. Set-up time before an exercise's first set follows the time until his Set-up done tap after 2 sessions in a row the same way. Rest times are never changed here: they are part of the plan. The start page lists what changed under Times set from your pace; Settings has the switch and Start over. Nothing extra is stored: it is worked out from the sessions each time. The numbers are in rules.json under pacing.

parts.name: Architecture tab
parts.description: Draws this diagram from architecture.json and lists every part with its description. The search box filters parts and flows by any word. If a part is added, removed or renamed in code, this file changes in the same commit and the spec doc's diagram is redrawn to match.

parts.name: Guided session screen
lines: the set, what's next, the clock
parts.description: What Cameron sees at the gym: the current exercise, set number, target weight and reps, effort target, a countdown or count-up, what comes next, and the session clock. v1.5: Pause in the header, a Set-up done tap before each new block, Equipment taken, finisher exercises in the top bar, and a last-set card kept apart from Up next. v1.14: on a work set the weight is the one big number with reps and effort on a line under it; cues fold away after an exercise's first set; the buttons stay at the bottom of the screen; Undo on the last-set card and after Skip or Equipment taken; Android Back opens the workout menu; the phone's status bar takes the phase color. v1.18: one screen with no scrolling at Android sizes and three-digit weights never cut; a readable top row; the coming sets with weight and reps; the whole plan one tap away; a red screen and button while paused with the gym clock still running; Left and Right boxes for work done one side at a time; a Ready tap before bar set-ups and the stretches.

parts.name: Progress: sessions and exercises
parts.description: The Log tab lists past sessions (tap for all sets and what changed) and, in its Exercises view, every exercise with its sets by date, PR markers and an estimated-1RM trend line. The Home screen shows next targets (editable) and a Benchmarks table for the seven benchmark lifts: the benchmark you entered (a set of 5 with 2 reps left), current estimated 1RM, and the next target the plan derives from it. v1.15: Home has one Main lifts card for the seven benchmark lifts (next weight x reps, e1RM; tap to change a target or enter a benchmark); every other lift's target shows in Targets today on its session's start page. v1.9: the Log tab moved inside Progress as Sessions and Exercises next to Overview. v1.14: swipe a session left to delete it, with Undo. v1.18.1: a set the timer logged shows Rate in the session's sets, and Rate the set the timer logged opens the first one.

parts.name: Progress page
parts.description: The Progress tab, laid out for a computer screen and still usable on the phone: which planned lifts are done, ended early or missed in each of the 12 weeks, a chart of estimated 1RM per benchmark lift from each session's best set, personal records, work sets per week and each accessory's first and latest top set. It reads saved sessions and runs; it changes nothing. On a computer it offers Load backup file, which puts the phone's backup into that browser. v1.9: with one session a lift card shows the best set and the next target instead of a lone dot; clicking a card opens every set of that lift; a card for work sets per muscle group this week against what the plan holds and a 10-set mark (data/muscles.json); sync status moved to the header. v1.14: explanations sit behind (i) buttons; Home has three week rings (js/rings.js: lifts, runs, hard efforts; rules.json weekRings). v1.18: the plan's runs sit in the 12-week grid under the lifts (done, missed, this week), and a Running card shows miles per week with the number of runs, total miles, the longest run and the latest pace.

parts.name: Plan tab
lines: this week, each session with its
parts.description: The Plan tab (v1.9): the 12 weeks and their phases, this week day by day, every session as planned with the next target for each lift and its rest, the runs, the goals in order and the coach check-in thread (the only thing it writes). It reads plan.json, goals.json and what the app stores. v1.18.3: on the phone it is four tabs, Week, Sessions, Goals and Check-ins; Sessions shows one lift session or the runs at a time and opens on the next session not logged yet, and tapping a day on Week opens that day's session. A computer 1000 px or wider shows everything on one page in two columns.

parts.name: Runs page
lines: this week's two runs and what each
asks for, miles by week, every run
parts.description: The Runs tab (rebuilt in v1.10). This week's planned runs with what each asks for: the interval set for the week and the long-run distance, one step past the longest long run so far (both from the numbers on plan.json runs). v1.18.4: the intervals go by pace (each stage has its own, intervals[].pace) with heart rate as the check (run.hr: fastEnd, easyUnder), and the long run by heart rate (run.hr.easy); no RPE. Each shows done with its numbers once a run is logged for it. Below: miles by week across the block (bike and ski distance left out, rules.json runLog), and every run with distance, time, pace and heart rate. Opening a run shows the watch's numbers and takes effort and what it counts as in one tap. Log a run takes time as 27:30. Garmin status, Check now and set-up sit under the heading. From v1.12 a run done on another day counts for the planned run it replaces, and a run not done yet says which days still work (rules.json runSchedule, never a lift day); Home shows it on the day it moved to. v1.18.1: a run from Garmin counts for a planned run only after Count it. The planned run's card (here and on Home, also on the day it moved to) lists this week's Garmin runs it could be, with Count it and Side run (an easy run that no planned run asks about again), and the run sheet says it counts toward miles only and offers the planned runs it could count for. A run typed in by hand counts as before. The computer only views, so it shows no Count it.

parts.name: Backup and export
lines: JSON to Drive via share sheet,
sheet in the Log tab layout
parts.description: Back up opens the Android share sheet with the backup JSON so Cameron can save it to Drive > Training in one tap; Download saves it on a PC. Export builds an .xlsx with a Log sheet and a Runs sheet in the same columns as the Excel log, using SheetJS vendored in the repo. v1.18.1: Restore runs the one-time upgrades on a backup from an older version (js/upgrade.js).

parts.name: Sync to your private repo
parts.description: Optional, off until set up in Settings. Keeps one file (tracker-data.json, the same content as a backup) in a private GitHub repo that belongs to Cameron. The phone uploads a few seconds after every saved session, run, target or settings change, and retries when signal returns. A device set to Only views downloads the file when the app opens and never uploads. The repo name and token are stored on the device only and are not part of a backup. The app refuses a public repo, and an empty phone loads the existing copy instead of overwriting it. Nothing is written to the app's own repo. v1.9: the header shows sync status with a refresh button. Both devices also read coach.json from the same repo (written by the coach review); only the phone applies its adjustments, once each. v1.18.1: a device that loads the file runs the one-time upgrades on it when it came from an older version.
